question.leadin: Answer the following questions about famous British explorers who died or disappeared while on their voyages.
question.text: This explorer gave the name Botany Bay to where he landed in Australia in 1770. This captain of the HMS Endeavour was killed by Hawaiian natives on his third voyage.
question.clue: The naturalists Daniel Solander and Joseph Banks accompanied this man on that voyage, during which this explorer visited Botany Bay.

swap.leadin: This country formed an army corps with Australia that fought in the Gallipoli campaign and is honored on ANZAC Day.
swap.text: Name this country, the location of silver ferns, which are featured on its airline's planes and its coat of arms. This island country, whose capital is Wellington, is located southeast of Australia.
swap.clue: In 1893 it became the first country to have universal women's suffrage, and it earlier saw a gold rush centered on Dunedin ("doo-nay-din").

question.leadin: Give the following the 1840 Treaty of Waitangi [why-tahn-gee].
question.text: The treaty was written by British colonizers and purposefully mistranslated when described to leaders of this ethnic group, which didn't intend to give up all sovereignty to the British. Western contact with these people led to a period of infighting called the Musket Wars.
question.answerHtml: Maori people (prompt on, but do not otherwise reveal, answers related to “indigenous New Zealanders”)
question.clue: Tribes of this people experienced bitter infighting in the Musket Wars.

swap.leadin: This kingdom's Law of the Splintered Paddle allowed all civilians to travel in peace.
swap.text: Name this kingdom, which was ruled from ʻIolani Palace. Sanford Dole helped overthrow this kingdom's last ruler, Queen Liliʻuokalani [luh-lee-uh-wo-kuh-LAA-nee].
swap.clue: An attempt to replace the Bayonet Constitution led to the overthrow of this kingdom by a group including Sanford Dole.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about American leaders involved in the Pacific Theatre of World War II.
question.text: Nimitz also participated in this battle, which is often considered to be the turning point of the Pacific Theatre. The Aleutian Islands Campaign was intended as a diversion from this battle, where the USS Yorktown and all four Japanese aircraft carriers that took part in the battle were sunk.
question.clue: The illness of William Halsey forced Raymond Spruance to take on an unfamiliar command role in this battle, which saw SBD Dauntless Dive Bombers from the Hornet help sink the Mikuma.

swap.text: In 1818, thousands of Pacific Islanders in this archipelago tattooed on themselves the name of their King Kamehameha. Kamehameha had earlier passed the Law of the Broken Paddle after uniting this archipelago and moving its capital to Honolulu.
swap.answerHtml: Hawaiian Islands [accept Mokupuni o Hawai‘i; prompt on the Sandwich Islands]
swap.clue: This region was forcibly* annexed by the United States in 1898.

question.text: The First Fleet initially landed at this location, but found it to be unsuitable and sailed to Port Jackson instead. James Cook first made landfall in Australia at this location.
question.clue: Fed by the Georges and Cooks Rivers, its north shore is home to Kingsford Smith airport.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the German colonial empire in the Pacific Ocean.
swap.text: This Pacific island country became a German protectorate after Albert Ellis discovered phosphate mines on it. Its status of abuse by the rest of the world continues, as Australia uses it to hoard unwanted refugees.
swap.clue: In 2016, Iranian Omid Masoumali set himself on fire while in this country.

question.text: This monarch of another short-lived country was deposed outside the ʻIolani Palace by American-backed revolutionaries. This monarch opposed a king's signing of the Bayonet Constitution.
question.clue: John L. Stevens was found to support anti-royalist conspirators in a report finding that the overthrow of this ruler was illegal, named for James H. Blount.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the economic history of sandalwood.
swap.text: In the early 19th century, sandalwood was the chief export of this kingdom, which the Chinese called "Tan Heong Shan," meaning "fragrant sandalwood mountains". Sugar planters backed the Bayonet Constitution in the final years of this kingdom's independence.
swap.clue: Its final ruler was forced to sign Lorrin Thurston's Bayonet Constitution, and this kingdom was succeeded by a republic led by Sanford Dole.

question.text: This New Zealand prime minister, the second woman to hold the office, officially apologized to Samoa in 2002 for injustices during colonial rule. This prime minister also introduced the controversial Foreshore and Seabed Act.

swap.text: Due to a similar story, seven of these figures at Ahu Akivi are thought to depict seven scouts who discovered Rapa Nui. Those examples of these figures are the only ones on Rapa Nui to face the ocean.
swap.answerHtml: moai [prompt on Easter Island heads or Easter Island statues]
swap.clue: A system of ropes likely allowed these objects to "walk" from Rano Raraku to ahu platforms.

question.leadin: This country's Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka was nicknamed "Colonel Steve Rambo" after his tendency to quote the Sylvester Stallone movie Rambo to describe a 1987 coup against Timoci Bavadra.
question.text: Name this country whose first indigenous prime minister Kamisese Mara attempted to seize power from Mahendra Chaudhry, who descended from the girmityas, during a coup led by George Speight in 2000.
question.answerHtml: Fiji [or Republic of Fiji; or Matanitu Tugalala o Viti]
question.clue: After removing Laisenia Qarase (un-guh-RAH-seh) from power, Frank Bainimarama became this country's prime minister.

swap.text: Scholars have suggested that only the introduction of sweet potato, which supplanted taro and yam, was sufficient to facilitate the labor needed to build many ahu and moai on this island after 1200 CE.
swap.clue: Wooden tablets discovered at this place depict glyphs written in reverse boustrophedon style, the rongorongo script.

question.leadin: Olaf Nelson took over this people's independence movement after its previous leader, Lealofi III of the Tupua Tamasese, was shot and killed by colonial police on Black Saturday, 1929.
question.text: Name this ethnic group whose rival matai chiefs sought backing from the US, UK, and Germany during their 1887 to 1889 "crisis." New Zealand apologized for its role in spreading the 1918 flu pandemic among this people.
question.answerHtml: Sāmoans [or tagata Sāmoa; accept Western Sāmoans; accept American Sāmoans; prompt on Polynesians]
question.clue: That civil war was written about in the book A Footnote to History, by a man who resided at Villa Vailima.

swap.leadin: A leader of this expedition beat Charles Gray after Gray stole skilligolee (SKIL-ee-goh-lee) porridge and contracted dysentery.
swap.text: Name this failed 1860s expedition which is commemorated on the Dig Tree. The Irish soldier John King was the only man to successfully see this expedition to fruition.
swap.answerHtml: Burke and Wills expedition [or answers describing the expedition of Robert O'Hara Burke and William John Wills; or Victorian Exploring Expedition]

question.text: This last King of Hawaii signed the Reciprocity Treaty of 1875 and was forced to sign the Bayonet Constitution. This brother of Liliʻuokalani names the last royal Hawaiian dynasty.

swap.leadin: In 1869, the HMS Rosario seized and freed victims of this practice aboard the Daphne.
swap.text: Name this practice of kidnapping Pacific Islanders to work on Australian plantations. In 2021, Bundaberg's mayor Jack Dempsey formally apologized for this practice, which may have affected over 100,000 people.
swap.clue: Louis Becke fictionalized his travels with Bully Hayes while he was engaging in this practice.

question.leadin: This man's premiership began after he ousted Laisenia Qarase in a 2006 coup.
question.text: Identify this naval commodore who served as Prime Minister of Fiji for 18 years. This man forced President Kaimese Mara to resign in 2000 during a so-called "coup within a coup" while Prime Minister Mahendra Chaudry and his cabinet were being held hostage by George Speight.

swap.text: The Catholic Social Studies Movement formed during the term of this first postwar Labor Prime Minister. Many European immigrants came to Australia during this man's term to work on the Snowy Mountains Scheme.
swap.clue: This Labor prime minister hired Hudson to draw initial plans for the Snowy Mountains Scheme and gave the "Light on the Hill" speech before losing power to Robert Menzies's Liberal-National coalition in 1949.
